```{r}
# Import the analysis datasets -------------------------------------------

# Main wide-format dataset containing participant characteristics,
# clinical variables, and questionnaire data.
# The Excel file is not included in the public repository because it

data_final_wide <- openxlsx::read.xlsx(
  "data/processed/data_wide_format.xlsx",
  sheet = 1
)


# Health care utilisation (HCU) dataset ----------------------------------
# Contains variables related to health care utilisation, including H12
# questionnaire data and HCU information.

data_HCU <- read.xlsx(
  "data/processed/data_HCU.xlsx",
  sheet = 1
)


# Time-to-event dataset ---------------------------------------------------
# Contains data used for the time-to-first-exacerbation analysis.

data_timetoevent <- read.xlsx(
  "data/processed/data_timetoevent.xlsx",
  sheet = 1
)

# Convert participant identifiers and treatment-group assignments to
# character variables to ensure consistent data types for subsequent
# data preparation and analyses.
data_timetoevent$patid <- as.character(data_timetoevent$patid)
data_timetoevent$arm <- as.character(data_timetoevent$arm)
```


# 1. Prepare the dataset for multiple imputation of secondary outcomes

```{r}
# Multiple imputation of secondary outcomes --------------------------------

# Select baseline characteristics, clinical variables, questionnaire
# scores, and follow-up measures needed for the imputation models.
data_wide_imp <- dplyr::select(
  data_final_wide,
  "patid",
  "arm",
  "STRgender_t0",
  "STRage_t0",
  "STRvar941_t0",
  "STRpred_main_mgN_t0",
  "STRbiological_none_t0",
  "H12pred_freq_t0",
  "H12ER_visit_t0",
  "H12hospitalization_freqN_t0",
  "FeNO",
  "BMI",
  "onset_late",
  "eos_high",
  "allergic",
  "CRSwNP",
  "CRSsNP",
  "IgET1_replaced",
  "ACQ_fu_day_t0",
  "ACQ_fu_day_t3",
  "ACQ_fu_day_t6",
  "ACQ_fu_day_t9",
  "ACQ_fu_day_t12",
  starts_with("ACQscore"),
  "CISF_fu_day_t0",
  "CISF_fu_day_t3",
  "CISF_fu_day_t6",
  "CISF_fu_day_t9",
  "CISF_fu_day_t12",
  starts_with("CISF_totscore"),
  "HCU_fu_day_t3",
  "HCU_fu_day_t6",
  "HCU_fu_day_t9",
  "HCU_fu_day_t12",
  starts_with("HCUER_visit"),
  starts_with("HCUhospitalization_frqN_"),
  starts_with("HCUpred_frq"),
  starts_with("HCUpred_main"),
  starts_with("HCUbiological_use")
)

# Add work productivity data from the WPAI subset.
data_wide_wpai <- dplyr::select(
  subset_wpai,
  "patid",
  "activity_impairment_perc_t0",
  "activity_impairment_perc_t3",
  "activity_impairment_perc_t6",
  "activity_impairment_perc_t9",
  "activity_impairment_perc_t12"
)

data_wide_imp <- left_join(
  data_wide_imp,
  data_wide_wpai,
  by = "patid"
)

# Add mAQLQ follow-up timing variables from the main dataset.
data_wide_aqlq_fuday <- dplyr::select(
  data_final_wide,
  "patid",
  "mAQLQ_fu_day_t0",
  "mAQLQ_fu_day_t3",
  "mAQLQ_fu_day_t6",
  "mAQLQ_fu_day_t9",
  "mAQLQ_fu_day_t12"
)

# Add mAQLQ total scores from the questionnaire subset.
data_wide_aqlq <- dplyr::select(
  subset_AQLQ,
  "patid",
  starts_with("mAQLQtotal")
)

data_wide_imp <- left_join(
  data_wide_imp,
  data_wide_aqlq_fuday,
  by = "patid"
)

data_wide_imp <- left_join(
  data_wide_imp,
  data_wide_aqlq,
  by = "patid"
)

# Add HADS follow-up timing variables and anxiety/depression scores.
data_wide_hads_fuday <- dplyr::select(
  data_final_wide,
  "patid",
  "HADS_fu_day_t0",
  "HADS_fu_day_t6",
  "HADS_fu_day_t12"
)

data_wide_hads <- dplyr::select(
  subset_HADS,
  "patid",
  starts_with("HADS_D_"),
  starts_with("HADS_A_")
)

data_wide_imp <- left_join(
  data_wide_imp,
  data_wide_hads_fuday,
  by = "patid"
)

data_wide_imp <- left_join(
  data_wide_imp,
  data_wide_hads,
  by = "patid"
)

# If baseline maintenance oral corticosteroid use was recorded as "no"
# and the dose is missing, assign a dose of zero.
data_wide_imp <- data_wide_imp %>%
  mutate(
    STRpred_main_mgN_t0 = ifelse(
      is.na(STRpred_main_mgN_t0) & STRvar941_t0 == "nee",
      0,
      STRpred_main_mgN_t0
    )
  )

# Remove variables that are not required for the imputation dataset.
data_wide_imp$STRvar941_t0 <- NULL
data_wide_imp$HCUpred_main_mg_t3 <- NULL
data_wide_imp$HCUpred_main_mgN_t3 <- NULL
data_wide_imp$HCUpred_main_mg_t6 <- NULL
data_wide_imp$HCUpred_main_mgN_t6 <- NULL
data_wide_imp$HCUpred_main_mg_t9 <- NULL
data_wide_imp$HCUpred_main_mgN_t9 <- NULL
data_wide_imp$HCUpred_main_mg_t12 <- NULL
data_wide_imp$HCUpred_main_mgN_t12 <- NULL
data_wide_imp$ACQscore <- NULL

# Identify variables treated as categorical in the imputation dataset.
factors <- c(
  "arm",
  "STRgender_t0",
  "STRbiological_none_t0",
  "HCUpred_main_t3",
  "HCUpred_main_t6",
  "HCUpred_main_t9",
  "HCUpred_main_t12",
  "HCUbiological_use_t3",
  "HCUbiological_use_t6",
  "HCUbiological_use_t9",
  "HCUbiological_use_t12",
  "FeNO",
  "onset_late",
  "eos_high",
  "allergic",
  "CRSwNP",
  "CRSsNP"
)

# Convert categorical variables to factors.
# The intermediate character conversion standardises their representation.
data_wide_imp <- data_wide_imp %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(factors), as.character))

data_wide_imp <- data_wide_imp %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(factors), as.factor))

# Rename baseline demographic and oral corticosteroid dose variables
# to shorter, more descriptive names.
data_wide_imp <- rename(
  data_wide_imp,
  sex = "STRgender_t0",
  age = "STRage_t0",
  predmainMG_baseline = "STRpred_main_mgN_t0"
)

# Recode the baseline biological-treatment checkbox response:
# "Checked" indicates no biological treatment, while "Unchecked"
# indicates biological treatment use.
data_wide_imp <- data_wide_imp %>%
  mutate(
    STRbiological_none_t0 = case_when(
      STRbiological_none_t0 == "Checked" ~ "Nee",
      STRbiological_none_t0 == "Unchecked" ~ "Ja",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )
```



# 1.1 Add follow-up exacerbation data

```{r}
# Import time-to-first-exacerbation data and the dataset containing
# weekly exacerbation information.
data_firstexa <- read.xlsx(
  "data/processed/timetoevent.xlsx",
  sheet = 1
)

data_EXAC <- read.xlsx(
  "data/processed/data_EXAC.xlsx",
  sheet = 1
)

# Calculate the number of distinct follow-up weeks available per participant.
data_EXAC <- data_EXAC %>%
  group_by(patid) %>%
  mutate(n_weeks_per_patient = n_distinct(fu_week)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Retain one row per participant and select the variables needed
# to merge exacerbation counts into the imputation dataset.
data_EXAC_1row <- data_EXAC %>%
  group_by(patid) %>%
  slice(1)

data_EXAC_1row <- data_EXAC_1row %>%
  select(
    patid,
    arm,
    total_n_exa,
    n_weeks_per_patient
  )

# Ensure the participant identifier and treatment group use compatible
# data types in both datasets before joining.
data_EXAC_1row$patid <- as.character(data_EXAC_1row$patid)
data_EXAC_1row$arm <- as.character(data_EXAC_1row$arm)

# Add exacerbation counts and follow-up duration to the imputation dataset.
data_wide_imp <- left_join(
  data_wide_imp,
  data_EXAC_1row,
  by = c("patid", "arm")
)

# Set the exacerbation count to missing when fewer than 40 distinct
# follow-up weeks are available, to avoid treating incomplete follow-up
# as a complete exacerbation count.
data_wide_imp <- data_wide_imp %>%
  mutate(
    severe_exacerbations_N = ifelse(
      n_weeks_per_patient < 40,
      NA,
      total_n_exa
    )
  )

# Remove the intermediate variables after deriving the analysis variable.
data_wide_imp$total_n_exa <- NULL
data_wide_imp$n_weeks_per_patient <- NULL
```


# 1.2 Save and reload the wide-format dataset

```{r}
# Save the prepared wide-format dataset for reuse in subsequent steps.
# The output contains participant-level data and will therefore not be committed
# to a public repository.
write.xlsx(

)

# Reload the saved dataset.
data_wide_imp <- read.xlsx(
  "data/processed/data_wide_imp.xlsx"
)
```

# 1.3 Reshape the dataset to long format and prepare variables

```{r}
# Reshape the imputation dataset to long format ---------------------------

# Convert repeated measurements from wide to long format.
# The timepoint suffix is extracted into a separate variable, while
# the shared variable name is retained as the column name.
data_long_imp <- data_wide_imp %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = matches("_t(0|3|6|9|12)$"),
    names_to = c(".value", "timepoint"),
    names_pattern = "(.*)_t(0|3|6|9|12)"
  )

# For baseline health care utilisation, use zero when the follow-up
# timing variable is missing.
data_long_imp <- data_long_imp %>%
  mutate(
    HCU_fu_day = ifelse(
      timepoint == 0 & is.na(HCU_fu_day),
      0,
      HCU_fu_day
    )
  )

# Fill missing baseline health care utilisation measures with the
# corresponding values collected at baseline.
data_long_imp <- data_long_imp %>%
  mutate(
    HCUpred_frq = ifelse(
      timepoint == 0 & is.na(HCUpred_frq),
      H12pred_freq,
      HCUpred_frq
    )
  )

data_long_imp <- data_long_imp %>%
  mutate(
    HCUER_visit = ifelse(
      timepoint == 0 & is.na(HCUER_visit),
      H12ER_visit,
      HCUER_visit
    )
  )

data_long_imp <- data_long_imp %>%
  mutate(
    HCUhospitalization_frqN = ifelse(
      timepoint == 0 & is.na(HCUhospitalization_frqN),
      H12hospitalization_freqN,
      HCUhospitalization_frqN
    )
  )

# Convert baseline biological-treatment status to a factor before
# using it to fill missing baseline follow-up values.
data_long_imp$STRbiological_none <- as.factor(
  data_long_imp$STRbiological_none
)

data_long_imp <- data_long_imp %>%
  mutate(
    HCUbiological_use = if_else(
      timepoint == 0 & is.na(HCUbiological_use),
      STRbiological_none,
      HCUbiological_use
    )
  )

# Recode biological-treatment use as 0/1.
data_long_imp <- data_long_imp %>%
  mutate(
    HCUbiological_use = case_when(
      HCUbiological_use == "Nee" ~ "0",
      HCUbiological_use == "Ja" ~ "1"
    )
  )

# Derive baseline maintenance oral corticosteroid use from the baseline
# dose when the corresponding follow-up variable is missing.
data_long_imp <- data_long_imp %>%
  mutate(
    HCUpred_main = case_when(
      is.na(HCUpred_main) &
        timepoint == 0 &
        predmainMG_baseline <= 0 ~ "nee",
      is.na(HCUpred_main) &
        timepoint == 0 &
        predmainMG_baseline > 0 ~ "ja",
      !is.na(HCUpred_main) ~ HCUpred_main
    )
  )

# Recode maintenance oral corticosteroid use as 0/1.
data_long_imp <- data_long_imp %>%
  mutate(
    HCUpred_main = case_when(
      HCUpred_main == "nee" ~ "0",
      HCUpred_main == "ja" ~ "1"
    )
  )

# Remove baseline variables that are no longer required after filling
# the corresponding long-format baseline values.
data_long_imp$STRbiological_none <- NULL
data_long_imp$H12hospitalization_freqN <- NULL
data_long_imp$H12ER_visit <- NULL
data_long_imp$H12pred_freq <- NULL

# Replace missing questionnaire timing values with the scheduled
# assessment day for each follow-up timepoint.
# These are nominal study days: baseline and approximately 12-week intervals.
data_long_imp <- data_long_imp %>%
  mutate(
    ACQ_fu_day = case_when(
      is.na(ACQ_fu_day) & timepoint == 0 ~ 0,
      is.na(ACQ_fu_day) & timepoint == 3 ~ 84,
      is.na(ACQ_fu_day) & timepoint == 6 ~ 168,
      is.na(ACQ_fu_day) & timepoint == 9 ~ 252,
      is.na(ACQ_fu_day) & timepoint == 12 ~ 336,
      TRUE ~ ACQ_fu_day
    )
  )

data_long_imp <- data_long_imp %>%
  mutate(
    mAQLQ_fu_day = case_when(
      is.na(mAQLQ_fu_day) & timepoint == 0 ~ 0,
      is.na(mAQLQ_fu_day) & timepoint == 3 ~ 84,
      is.na(mAQLQ_fu_day) & timepoint == 6 ~ 168,
      is.na(mAQLQ_fu_day) & timepoint == 9 ~ 252,
      is.na(mAQLQ_fu_day) & timepoint == 12 ~ 336,
      TRUE ~ mAQLQ_fu_day
    )
  )

data_long_imp <- data_long_imp %>%
  mutate(
    CISF_fu_day = case_when(
      is.na(CISF_fu_day) & timepoint == 0 ~ 0,
      is.na(CISF_fu_day) & timepoint == 3 ~ 84,
      is.na(CISF_fu_day) & timepoint == 6 ~ 168,
      is.na(CISF_fu_day) & timepoint == 9 ~ 252,
      is.na(CISF_fu_day) & timepoint == 12 ~ 336,
      TRUE ~ CISF_fu_day
    )
  )

data_long_imp <- data_long_imp %>%
  mutate(
    HADS_fu_day = case_when(
      is.na(HADS_fu_day) & timepoint == 0 ~ 0,
      is.na(HADS_fu_day) & timepoint == 6 ~ 168,
      is.na(HADS_fu_day) & timepoint == 12 ~ 336,
      TRUE ~ HADS_fu_day
    )
  )

data_long_imp <- data_long_imp %>%
  mutate(
    HCU_fu_day = case_when(
      is.na(HCU_fu_day) & timepoint == 0 ~ 0,
      is.na(HCU_fu_day) & timepoint == 3 ~ 84,
      is.na(HCU_fu_day) & timepoint == 6 ~ 168,
      is.na(HCU_fu_day) & timepoint == 9 ~ 252,
      is.na(HCU_fu_day) & timepoint == 12 ~ 336,
      TRUE ~ HCU_fu_day
    )
  )

# Convert count variables and the timepoint to numeric values.
data_long_imp$HCUhospitalization_frqN <- as.numeric(
  data_long_imp$HCUhospitalization_frqN
)

data_long_imp$HCUER_visit <- as.numeric(
  data_long_imp$HCUER_visit
)

data_long_imp$HCUpred_frq <- as.numeric(
  data_long_imp$HCUpred_frq
)

data_long_imp$timepoint <- as.numeric(
  data_long_imp$timepoint
)
```



# 1.4 Specify the multilevel imputation models

```{r}
# Specify methods and predictors for multilevel multiple imputation -----

# The cluster identifier must be integer-valued for the selected
# multilevel imputation methods.
data_long_imp$patid <- as.integer(data_long_imp$patid)

# Set the imputation method for each variable.
meth <- make.method(data_long_imp)

# Binary time-varying variables: multilevel joint modelling.
meth[c("HCUpred_main", "HCUbiological_use")] <- "2l.jomo"

# Continuous or count time-varying variables: multilevel normal models.
meth[c(
  "ACQscore",
  "mAQLQtotal",
  "CISF_totscore",
  "HADS_D",
  "HADS_A",
  "HCUER_visit",
  "HCUpred_frq",
  "HCUhospitalization_frqN",
  "activity_impairment_perc",
  "severe_exacerbations_N"
)] <- "2l.pan"

# Time-fixed categorical variables: predictive mean matching at the
# participant level.
meth[c(
  "arm",
  "sex",
  "FeNO",
  "onset_late",
  "eos_high",
  "allergic",
  "CRSwNP",
  "CRSsNP"
)] <- "2lonly.pmm"

# Time-fixed continuous variables: normal imputation at the
# participant level.
meth[c(
  "age",
  "predmainMG_baseline",
  "BMI",
  "IgET1_replaced"
)] <- "2lonly.norm"

# Check that the method vector matches the columns of the dataset.
all(names(meth) == colnames(data_long_imp)) # Expected: TRUE

# Create the predictor matrix, which specifies which variables predict
# each variable being imputed.
pred <- make.predictorMatrix(data_long_imp)

# Mark participant ID as the clustering variable in the two-level models.
pred[, "patid"] = -2

# Specify a random slope for time for selected time-varying outcomes.
pred[c(
  "ACQscore",
  "mAQLQtotal",
  "CISF_totscore",
  "HADS_D",
  "HADS_A",
  "activity_impairment_perc",
  "HCUER_visit",
  "HCUpred_frq",
  "HCUhospitalization_frqN"
), "timepoint"] <- 2

# Exclude the questionnaire and HCU timing variables from the predictor
# matrix. These variables are retained as auxiliary information but are
# not used as predictors or imputation targets.
pred[, c(
  "ACQ_fu_day",
  "mAQLQ_fu_day",
  "CISF_fu_day",
  "HADS_fu_day",
  "HCU_fu_day"
)] = 0

pred[c(
  "ACQ_fu_day",
  "mAQLQ_fu_day",
  "CISF_fu_day",
  "HADS_fu_day",
  "HCU_fu_day"
), ] = 0

# Include cluster means of other time-varying outcomes as predictors
# in the imputation models for the listed outcomes.
pred[
  "ACQscore",
  c("mAQLQtotal", "CISF_totscore", "HADS_D", "HADS_A",
    "activity_impairment_perc")
] <- 3

pred[
  "mAQLQtotal",
  c("ACQscore", "CISF_totscore", "HADS_D", "HADS_A",
    "activity_impairment_perc")
] <- 3

pred[
  "CISF_totscore",
  c("ACQscore", "mAQLQtotal", "HADS_D", "HADS_A",
    "activity_impairment_perc")
] <- 3

pred[
  "HADS_D",
  c("ACQscore", "CISF_totscore", "mAQLQtotal", "HADS_A",
    "activity_impairment_perc")
] <- 3

pred[
  "HADS_A",
  c("ACQscore", "CISF_totscore", "HADS_D", "mAQLQtotal",
    "activity_impairment_perc")
] <- 3

pred[
  "activity_impairment_perc",
  c("ACQscore", "CISF_totscore", "HADS_D", "HADS_A",
    "mAQLQtotal")
] <- 3
```



# 1.5 Run and assess multiple imputation

```{r}
# Run multilevel multiple imputation -------------------------------------

# Generate 10 imputed datasets using 30 iterations per dataset.
# The seed ensures reproducibility.
imp <- mice(
  data_long_imp,
  m = 10,
  maxit = 30,
  seed = 2026,
  predictorMatrix = pred,
  method = meth
)

# Inspect any logged warnings or issues from the imputation process.
imp$loggedEvents

# Review trace plots and the distributions of imputed values.
plot(imp)

densityplot(
  imp,
  ~ ACQscore + CISF_totscore + mAQLQtotal +
    HADS_D + HADS_A + activity_impairment_perc
)

densityplot(
  imp,
  ~ HCUER_visit + HCUpred_frq + HCUhospitalization_frqN +
    severe_exacerbations_N
)
```

```{r}
  header = TRUE
)
```


# 2. Multiple imputation for the time-to-event analysis

```{r}
# Multiple imputation: time-to-event analysis -----------------------------

# Study context:
# Randomised controlled trial comparing control and intervention.
# Primary outcome: time to first severe asthma exacerbation over 48 weeks.
#
# Approach:
# Use risk-score imputation to address potentially informative censoring
# among participants censored before the 48-week data cutoff. Fit Cox
# regression models to the imputed datasets and pool the results.
#
# Important: this approach relies on assumptions about the relationship
# between early censoring and the underlying risk of an exacerbation.
```


# 2.1 Set up the analysis dataset

```{r}
# Merge time-to-event outcomes with baseline covariates.
# The join uses participant ID and treatment arm.
data_wide_imp_timetoevent <- left_join(
  data_wide_imp,
  data_timetoevent,
  by = c("patid", "arm")
)

# Load the package used for risk-score imputation and the survival
# analysis functions.
# Install packages separately if they are not already available.
# install.packages("InformativeCensoring")

library(InformativeCensoring)
library(survival)
```



# 2.2 Classify censoring type

```{r}
# Classify censoring for the InformativeCensoring package ---------------

# Censoring categories:
# 0 = observed event
# 1 = censored before the 48-week data cutoff; treated as potentially
#     informatively censored and eligible for imputation
# 2 = censored at or after the 48-week cutoff; treated as administrative
#     censoring and not imputed
#
# The data cutoff (DCO) is set to 48 weeks.
data_wide_imp_timetoevent$DCO.time <- 48

# Flag participants censored before the data cutoff for imputation.
data_wide_imp_timetoevent <- data_wide_imp_timetoevent %>%
  mutate(
    to.impute = case_when(
      status == 0 & time < 48 ~ TRUE,
      TRUE ~ FALSE
    )
  )

# Assign the censoring category based on event status and follow-up time.
data_wide_imp_timetoevent <- data_wide_imp_timetoevent %>%
  mutate(
    censor.type = case_when(
      status == 1 ~ 0,
      status == 0 & time < 48 ~ 1,
      status == 0 & time >= 48 ~ 2
    )
  )
```


# 2.3 Prepare data for imputation

```{r}
# Prepare data for risk-score imputation ---------------------------------

# Set the random seed for reproducibility.
set.seed(2026)

# Select variables required for the imputation and survival analyses.
test <- select(
  data_wide_imp_timetoevent,
  arm,
  FeNO,
  sex,
  age,
  eos_high,
  H12pred_freq_t0,
  status,
  time,
  patid,
  DCO.time,
  to.impute,
  censor.type
)

# Create an adjusted follow-up time:
# - Set time zero to one week.
# - Cap times beyond the 48-week data cutoff at 48 weeks.
test <- test %>%
  mutate(
    time_adj = case_when(
      time == 0 ~ 1,
      time > 48 ~ 48,
      TRUE ~ time
    ),
    .after = time
  )

# Convert treatment arm, FeNO, and sex to factors for model fitting.
test$arm <- factor(as.character(test$arm))
test$FeNO <- factor(as.character(test$FeNO))
test$sex <- as.factor(test$sex)

# Create numeric versions of binary predictors for use in ScoreImpute.
# Numeric coding avoids potential factor-level problems in bootstrap
# samples where a category may be absent.
test$arm_num <- as.numeric(as.character(test$arm))
test$FeNO_num <- as.numeric(as.character(test$FeNO))
test$eos_num <- as.numeric(as.character(test$eos_high))

# Check the relationship between the imputation flag and censoring type.
# Participants flagged for imputation should have censor.type == 1.
table(test$to.impute, test$censor.type)

# Inspect the records flagged for imputation.
filter(test, to.impute == TRUE)
```

 
# 2.4 Specify the variable mapping and perform risk-score imputation

```{r}
# Map dataset columns to the variable names expected by the package.
col.control <- col.headings(
  arm = "arm",
  has.event = "status",
  time = "time_adj",
  Id = "patid",
  DCO.time = "DCO.time",
  to.impute = "to.impute",
  censor.type = "censor.type"
)

# Risk-score imputation ---------------------------------------------------

# ScoreImpute uses an event model to estimate risk scores and bootstrap
# resampling to reflect uncertainty when imputing event times for
# participants censored before the data cutoff.
#
# The imputation model includes treatment arm, FeNO, eosinophil category,
# age, sex, and prior exacerbation frequency.
#
# An unstratified bootstrap is used here. The number of imputed datasets
# is set to 10.
imp_cox <- ScoreImpute(
  test,
  event.model = ~ arm_num + FeNO_num + eos_num + age + sex + H12pred_freq_t0,
  col.control = col.control,
  bootstrap.strata = rep(1, nrow(test)),
  m = 10
)

# Inspect any warnings or logged issues from the imputation.
imp_cox$logged.events

# Extract and inspect the first imputed dataset.
# impute.time and impute.event contain the survival time and event status
# used for the imputed analysis.
imp1 <- ExtractSingle(imp_cox, index = 1)

imp1$data %>%
  filter(to.impute == TRUE) %>%
  select(
    patid,
    arm_num,
    FeNO_num,
    time_adj,
    impute.time,
    impute.event
  )
```


# 2.5 Fit and pool Cox models

```{r}
# Fit Cox models and pool results across imputed datasets ---------------

# The analysis model includes treatment arm and FeNO.
# FeNO was used to stratify randomisation.
#
# ImputeStat pools estimates across the imputed datasets.
imputed.fits <- ImputeStat(
  imp_cox,
  formula = ~ arm + FeNO,
  method = "Cox"
)

# Review the pooled model results.
summary(imputed.fits)

# Inspect estimates and variance information from the imputed datasets.
imputed.fits$statistics

# Calculate the hazard ratio and 95% confidence interval from the
# specified log hazard ratio and its variance.
# These values are entered directly rather than extracted automatically
# from the pooled model object.
log_hr <- 0.0176726
var_log_hr <- 0.03875343

hr <- exp(log_hr)

ci_lower <- exp(log_hr - 1.96 * sqrt(var_log_hr))
ci_upper <- exp(log_hr + 1.96 * sqrt(var_log_hr))

hr
ci_lower
ci_upper
```


# 2.6 Assess the proportional hazards assumption

```{r}
# Assess the proportional hazards assumption -----------------------------

# Assess proportional hazards separately in each imputed dataset.
# The Cox model uses the imputed event time and event indicator.
ph_tests <- lapply(1:imp$m, function(i) {
  d <- ExtractSingle(imp, index = i)

  fit <- coxph(
    Surv(impute.time, impute.event) ~ arm + FeNO,
    data = d$data
  )

  cox.zph(fit, transform = "km")
})

# Inspect the proportional hazards tests for each imputed dataset.
lapply(ph_tests, print)
```


# 2.7 Compare the original and imputed survival models

```{r}
# Compare survival models before and after imputation --------------------

# Fit a Cox model to the original event and censoring times.
fit_original <- coxph(
  Surv(time_adj, status) ~ arm + FeNO,
  data = test
)

summary(fit_original)

# Fit the same covariate model using the imputed survival time and
# event indicator from the first imputed dataset.
fit_imp1 <- coxph(
  Surv(impute.time, impute.event) ~ arm + FeNO,
  data = imp1$data
)

summary(fit_imp1)
```
